statement: On E:y²+y=x³−1 with R=(1,0), U=E−E[3], the actual joint compact/j-line level-three quotient admits a Selmer lift of aκ(R), for an exponent a differing from an integer n at only finitely many coefficient primes, if and only if a=n. In particular every nonzero finite-support exponent is excluded, completing the baseline-zero case.

notes: Zero-primary Chebotarev puts the global quadratic flex-unit radical into the joint proper division tower. Every quadratic character kills odd translation factors; a residual C3 at2 kills the2-translation lattice by Cayley–Hamilton, so a quadratic extension over the chosen base inside the tower must lie in the abelian CM torsion field. Explicit2-torsion value over Q(ζ,∛2) is nonsquare at31 and has cubic norm1, so its radical is not Galois over Qζ. For everyp>=5, full Cartan inertia and disjointness give a torsion orbit of at least24; an exact modulo4 calculation makes square values zeros of a nonzero function with pole order23. Cubic b-conjugation again gives norm1 and a non-Galois radical. Prescribed-primary Frobenius then contradicts local Selmer compatibility for any finite support containing that prime. Pure3 is A68. Root and B independently audited the field and local-polynomial arguments. No arbitrary infinite-alteration or finite-quotient-fibre classification is claimed.
